comparator.name: International Business Administration
comparator.academicYear: Current public curriculum; year 2 applies from 2025–26 and year 3 from 2026–27
comparator.sourceNotes: The official study-programme pages specify ten required 6-EC courses in year one (60 EC), ten required 6-EC courses in year two (60 EC), three required 6-EC courses in year three (18 EC), a genuine 30-EC flexibility window, and a 12-EC IBA thesis: 180 EC in all. The third-year window is kept as open choice, not portrayed as compulsory named subject content. The year-three page applies from academic year 2026–27; the year-two page applies from 2025–26.
components: Genuine 30-EC choice space in the published third year, including electives, internship or exchange, rather than a fixed major or compulsory named course.
Compulsory independent thesis in International Business Administration.

core: International management, business strategy, marketing and global organisational decisions
Business economics, accounting, finance and legal context
Organisational design, human behaviour, leadership, culture and work
Quantitative and qualitative business research and academic analysis
adjacent: Responsible organisations, sustainable entrepreneurship and social-environmental value
Business analytics, digitalisation and innovation using computational data methods
questions: How can organisations adapt strategy and operations to social, environmental and digital change?

alternatives.label: International management and organisational strategy
alternatives.concept: A broad management curriculum connects international strategy and governance with accounting, finance, economics, law, marketing, organisational behaviour, leadership and quantitative and qualitative research. Its social-science methods complement Radboud’s integrated organisational curriculum; UCR does not reproduce the compulsory Global Value Chains or IBA thesis sequence.
alternatives.labelReason: The title names the dominant course sequence: cross-border business and organisational strategy with economics, management and research methods.
progression: All formal prerequisites precede dependent courses and every selected course is planned in its assigned semester. Introductory business and methods courses establish foundations; advanced courses follow the applicable gateway and research-methods courses. Personal & Professional Development occurs in year one.
traceOverrides: uses consumer research, team product development and cost analysis to practice entrepreneurship in an organisational setting
teaches business strategy and strategic change in digital markets
examines how AI adoption changes firms, workers, innovation and governance through business cases

alternatives.label: Responsible enterprise and sustainable change
alternatives.concept: A responsible-enterprise curriculum joins entrepreneurship and organisational leadership to climate, circular-economy assessment and sustainability governance. It studies the environmental constraints and social value of business decisions through both management and environmental-science courses; specialist IBA value-chain and thesis requirements remain distinct.
alternatives.labelReason: The title names the dominant course sequence: sustainable enterprise with climate, circular-economy and governance courses.
progression: All formal prerequisites precede dependent courses and every selected course is planned in its assigned semester. Introductory business and methods courses establish foundations; advanced courses follow the applicable gateway and research-methods courses. Personal & Professional Development occurs in year one.
alternatives.distinctness: Six course replacements (45 EC) shift the first programme toward environmental science, life-cycle assessment, sustainability governance and public economics; these implement the named responsible-enterprise evidence and change the academic work, not merely the title.
traceOverrides: uses consumer research, team product development and cost analysis to practice entrepreneurship in an organisational setting
teaches business strategy and strategic change in digital markets
examines how AI adoption changes firms, workers, innovation and governance through business cases

alternatives.label: Business analytics and digital innovation
alternatives.concept: A digital-business curriculum combines strategy, finance, markets and organisations with programming, databases, mathematical methods, data science, machine learning and AI ethics. The computational sequence provides practical data skills behind digital innovation while leaving Radboud’s independent IBA thesis and detailed organisational requirements distinct.
alternatives.labelReason: The title names the dominant course sequence: business decisions with a substantial programming, data and AI sequence.
progression: All formal prerequisites precede dependent courses and every selected course is planned in its assigned semester. Introductory business and methods courses establish foundations; advanced courses follow the applicable gateway and research-methods courses. Personal & Professional Development occurs in year one.
alternatives.distinctness: The programming, database, data-science, machine-learning, deep-learning, mathematics and AI-ethics sequence changes the actual methods of study. It differs by nine courses (67.5 EC) from management and by eleven (82.5 EC) from sustainable enterprise, and both differences implement the evidenced digital expertise direction.
traceOverrides: uses consumer research and product prototyping to connect market needs to business decisions
examines the ethics and social impacts of AI applications in organisations

selection.assessment: The broad international-management curriculum is the closest match. Responsible enterprise has a distinct environmental and governance course sequence. Business analytics develops a separate technical data and AI sequence. All three meet evidence, coherence, pairwise distinctness and semester feasibility, so the three-alternative maximum is reached.

blocks: Both introduce entrepreneurship and business organisations; Radboud puts international context at the centre.
Both teach marketing decisions and engagement with consumers; Radboud also integrates strategy.
Both analyse the functioning of organisations; UCR emphasises psychology of leadership.
Both consider creating value through enterprise; UCR’s team product design includes explicit sustainability analysis.
Both address managing people in organisations; UCR focuses on diversity management rather than the full HRM function.
Both address organisational design and adaptation; UCR situates change in AI adoption and its business implications.
Both treat international coordination and governance across business actors; UCR does not cover the full value-chain sequence.
Both develop strategy for changing competitive and international business environments; UCR emphasises digital transformation.
Both analyse international-market and consumer evidence; UCR teaches market research rather than all international-marketing functions.
Both apply strategic reasoning to organisational decisions; UCR uses negotiation simulations.
Both develop capacities for leading organisational change, with UCR taking a personal leadership perspective.
No scheduled UCR course directly covers the specifically credited System Theory component at comparable scope; it remains distinct.
Both introduce economic reasoning for business settings.
Both teach accounting and organisational finance.
Both investigate finance for organisational decisions; UCR also covers money and banking.
Both support academic and professional development, though UCR emphasises personal and professional reflection.
Both develop quantitative research design and statistical analysis.
Both teach qualitative social research methods applicable to organisations.
Both advance quantitative analysis; UCR teaches econometric modelling rather than a general business-methods sequence.
Both address using data in digital organisations; UCR teaches technical data manipulation rather than organisation-wide innovation management.
No scheduled UCR course directly covers the specifically credited Bachelor’s Thesis IBA component at comparable scope; it remains distinct.
Both examine organisational responsibilities to external stakeholders; UCR concentrates on public and multi-actor sustainability governance.
Both study the ethical consequences of organisational choices; UCR’s case domain is AI rather than international business.
Both evaluate economic trade-offs in responsible organisational decisions; UCR focuses on public-economics mechanisms.
No scheduled UCR course directly covers the specifically credited Flexibility window component at comparable scope; it remains distinct.

notes.text: The UCR alternatives can share international strategy, marketing, economics, organisational behaviour and business research with Radboud while concentrating differently on sustainable enterprise or technical analytics. Radboud’s prescribed Global Value Chains, Systems Theory and independent IBA thesis remain separate requirements; the 30-EC third-year flexibility window is genuine choice space.
